description.en: For years the Vue community has wanted native app development on par with React Native. Lynx set out to democratize cross platform technology when it open sourced, and Evan You backed the idea. With AI writing the code, the engineering effort is no longer the obstacle, and "Vue + Lynx = Vue Native" is real. The talk runs Vue Lynx apps live in the deck and walks through the dual threaded design that keeps Vue on the background thread, instant first frame rendering, and where Vapor mode fits.
description.zh: 长久以来，Vue 社区一直期盼拥有比肩 React Native 的原生应用开发能力。Lynx 开源时就确立了普惠跨平台技术的愿景，也得到了尤雨溪等框架作者的支持。如今借助 AI 的码力，工程体量不再是阻碍，「Vue + Lynx = Vue Native」终于不再只是愿景。演讲在幻灯片里现场运行 Vue Lynx 应用，讲解让 Vue 留在后台线程的双线程设计、瞬时首帧渲染，以及 Vapor 模式在其中的位置。

description.en: A two-hour, hands-on workshop and hackathon I ran at WeAreDevelopers World Congress: vibe code one app and bring it to web, mobile and desktop with Lynx, then dig into what makes app infrastructure AI-native. The three principles from [GOSIM](commit:gosim-2026-vibe-native), put in people's hands.

details.en: "AI is changing how apps are built, but most apps are still built one platform at a time. In this small hands-on workshop and hackathon, you will explore Lynx, the cross-platform framework behind TikTok and CapCut. With Lynx, you can vibe code once and bring the same app experience to web, mobile, and desktop from a single codebase. Along the way, we'll also deep dive into how app infra such as Lynx is designed to be AI-native: AI-Ergonomic (harness-able), AI-Efficient (token-economical), and AI-Expressive (agent-generative UI)."

title.en: Vibe Native for More: Why AI Agents Deserve a Better App Framework
title.zh: Vibe Native for More: Why AI Agents Deserve a Better App Framework

description.en: My argument: AI is changing how apps are built, but not what they're built on, and an agent without a cross-platform framework has to write, verify and maintain every app once per platform. I laid out three principles for AI-native app infrastructure, AI-Ergonomic, AI-Efficient and AI-Expressive, and demoed [vue-lynx](https://github.com/Huxpro/vue-lynx), a full Vue 3 renderer for Lynx that I [vibe coded in two weeks](https://x.com/Huxpro/status/2036993665965416601).
description.zh: My argument: AI is changing how apps are built, but not what they're built on, and an agent without a cross-platform framework has to write, verify and maintain every app once per platform. I laid out three principles for AI-native app infrastructure, AI-Ergonomic, AI-Efficient and AI-Expressive, and demoed [vue-lynx](https://github.com/Huxpro/vue-lynx), a full Vue 3 renderer for Lynx that I [vibe coded in two weeks](https://x.com/Huxpro/status/2036993665965416601).

details.en: "AI is transforming how apps are built, but not what they're built on. Without a cross-platform framework, agents must generate, verify, and maintain separate code for every platform. This talk introduces Lynx, the open-source cross-platform framework powering TikTok and CapCut at billion-user scale, and our three principles for AI-native app infrastructure: AI-Ergonomic (harness-able), AI-Efficient (token-economical), and AI-Expressive (intent-driven UI). We demonstrate how vue-lynx — a full Vue 3 renderer for Lynx — was vibe-coded in two weeks as proof of this principle."
details.zh: "AI is transforming how apps are built, but not what they're built on. Without a cross-platform framework, agents must generate, verify, and maintain separate code for every platform. We demonstrate how vue-lynx — a full Vue 3 renderer for Lynx — was vibe-coded in two weeks as proof of this principle."

description.en: The Chinese edition of [React for Two Threads](commit:react-universe-2025-two-threads), with Ziqi Zhen and Haoyang Wang at SEE Conf 2025: Lynx's dual-threaded React, instant first frames, and what emerges once the UI thread is first class.

details.en: From the official recording: "For ten years we've been used to a world of single-threaded React. What if it hadn't been that way from the start? If React had been born dual-threaded, what would we unlock? What challenges would we meet? Would new features, abstractions and patterns emerge? Let's imagine it together; maybe it isn't just a fantasy."
details.zh: 「十年来，我们都习惯了「单线程 React」的世界，可如果它一开始就不是这样呢？假如 React 生来就是「双线程」，我们会解锁什么好处？又将遭遇哪些挑战？会有什么全新的特性、抽象和模式涌现出来吗？让我们一同想象一下，或许，这并非空想。」

title.en: Lynx: Making ByteDance Beat Across Platforms

description.en: [Lynx](commit:lynx-framework)'s open-source debut on stage. Three days after we open-sourced it, I told the 19th D2's cross-platform track why ByteDance opened up a framework it had grown for years, just as cross-platform approaches were converging, and what makes it different.
description.zh: [Lynx](commit:lynx-framework) 的开源首演。开源三天后，我在第十九届 D2 的跨端专场讲：在跨端思路趋同、格局固化之时，字节为什么把孕育多年的 Lynx 开源，它又和别人有什么不一样。

details.en: "As client products mature and fragment, cross-platform has become the default choice for many developers and companies. At the same time, UI framework innovation is converging, the approaches look more and more alike, and the market is settling into a fixed shape. Against that backdrop, why did Lynx, the cross-platform technology ByteDance nurtured for years, decide to go open source? This talk lifts the veil on Lynx and looks at the insights and the future of cross-platform together."
details.zh: 「伴随终端业务的成熟和碎片化，跨端已成为众多开发者和企业的首选。但同时，UI 框架的创新在收敛，跨端思路大同小异，市场格局趋于固化。在这个背景下，字节孕育多年的跨端技术 —— Lynx，为何决定走向开源？本演讲将揭开 Lynx 的“神秘面纱”，与你一同探寻跨端的洞见与未来。」

description.en: My first English talk at an in-person conference, three months after we open-sourced [Lynx](commit:lynx-framework). I walked React Summit through what makes Lynx familiar to React developers, what sets it apart, and how its dual-threaded design delivers instant launches and silky interactions.
description.zh: My first English talk at an in-person conference, three months after we open-sourced [Lynx](commit:lynx-framework). I walked React Summit through what makes Lynx familiar to React developers, what sets it apart, and how its dual-threaded design delivers instant launches and silky interactions.

details.en: "Lynx, a new cross-platform stack adopted by the TikTok app that empowers teams to ship truly native UIs to mobile and web from a single codebase using their existing web skills like CSS and React, has recently been open sourced. In this talk, we'll explore what makes Lynx familiar and what sets it apart from other cross-platform technologies; we'll take a closer look at its dual-threaded design, and how that enables Lynx's instant launches and silky-smooth interactions, plus a sneak peak at what's next for Lynx." ([GitNation](https://gitnation.com/contents/lynx-unlock-native-for-more))

description.en: For a decade React has lived on one JavaScript thread. With Ziqi Zhen and Haoyang Wang from the Lynx team, I asked what React looks like when it's born for two: what it unlocks, what it costs, which abstractions emerge. Not a thought experiment: it's how [ReactLynx](https://lynxjs.org/react/) runs today.
description.zh: For a decade React has lived on one JavaScript thread. With Ziqi Zhen and Haoyang Wang from the Lynx team, I asked what React looks like when it's born for two: what it unlocks, what it costs, which abstractions emerge. Not a thought experiment: it's how [ReactLynx](https://lynxjs.org/react/) runs today.

details.en: "For over a decade, we've lived in a universe where programming UIs with React on the client-side, from event handling to rendering, has been ruled by a single JavaScript thread. But what if React had been born differently? What if, from day one, it had been designed to fully embrace two threads? What benefits would that unlock? What challenges would we face? And what new features, abstractions, and patterns might emerge? What if this isn't just imagination... but something that exists today?"

And what new features, abstractions, and patterns might emerge? What if this isn't just imagination... but something that exists today?"

By taking advantage of Lynx's dual-threaded architecture, it offers high performance and native-graded interactivity. Join us to learn how we built it, and how it unlocks Lynx to scale across a massive range of products, even faster."

title.en: The Frontend Is Dead. Long Live the Frontend.

description.en: A main-stage keynote at Juejin's annual tech talks. In 2023 the hottest thing in frontend was the line "frontend is dead", so I modeled its turning points, big and small, to argue why frontend, as the bond between humans and machines, lives on, and what AI and the metaverse bring next. Over 200,000 views on Bilibili.
description.zh: 掘金年度技术演讲的主论坛主题演讲。2023 年聊起前端，最火的不是哪个框架，而是那句「前端已死」：我给前端史上的大小拐点建了个模型，推演前端作为人与机器的纽带为什么会「永生」，再看 AI 与元宇宙会带来什么。B 站 20 万播放。

commentary.en: Frontend as a job title may fade. Frontend as the bond between humans and machines will not.
commentary.zh: 作为岗位的前端或许会消亡，但作为人机交互纽带的前端不会。

details.en: In 2023 the hottest thing about frontend was not a framework. It was the line "frontend is dead." Looking back and ahead, in this constantly shifting digital world frontend has "died" before, and it will "die" again. Every leap, from PC to Web to mobile, and now as we stand at the edge of AI and the metaverse, the form may change, but frontend as the bond between humans and machines is eternal. This talk reviews the inflection points in that evolution, and looks ahead at what comes next.
details.zh: 2023 年聊起前端，最火的并不是哪个框架，而是那句「前端已死」。放眼过去和未来，在这个不断变化的数字世界里，前端不但「死」过，而且还一定会再「死」。每一次跃迁 —— 从 PC 到 Web 到移动时代，再到现在我们正站在 AI 的风口浪尖和元宇宙的边缘 —— 或许形式会不同，但前端作为人与机器纽带的本质是永恒的。本演讲将回顾大前端技术演化中的拐点，并对下一个世代的前端趋势做一些展望和猜想。

description.en: At the 6th FEDAY, the slot right before Evan You's closing talk: is frontend dead, or the future, and what do we even mean by frontend? After Qi Lu's talk on large models, I modeled its turning points and guessed at frontend, and frontend engineers, in an age of AI and AVXR. Two months later it grew into my [Juejin keynote](commit:juejin-talk-2023).
description.zh: 第六届 FEDAY，紧挨在尤雨溪闭幕演讲之前的一场：前端已死，还是前端未来？受陆奇博士大模型演讲的启发，我试着回答「我们说的前端到底是什么」，并猜想 AI、AVXR 时代的前端与前端工程师。两个月后，它长成了掘金的[主题演讲](commit:juejin-talk-2023)。

details.en: Is frontend dead, or is it the future? And when we say frontend, what are we actually talking about? Inspired by Qi Lu's talk on large models, a look at the inflection points in frontend's evolution, and a guess at what frontend (and frontend engineers) become in the next generation: AI, AVXR, and beyond.
details.zh: 前端已死，又或是前端未来？当我们在说前端时，我们又在说什么？受陆奇博士的大模型演讲启发，不妨我们也来探讨一些大前端技术演化中的拐点，对下个世代（ AI、AVXR …）的前端（工程师）做一点猜想。

description.en: A Vue 3 custom renderer for Lynx, built with AI over two weeks of evenings and weekends. The whole Vue runtime runs on Lynx's background thread and ships every DOM mutation to the main thread as one batch per tick, so Vue apps render native UI on iOS, Android, and the web. 852 of Vue's 949 upstream tests pass through that dual threaded pipeline.
description.zh: Lynx 的 Vue 3 自定义渲染器，用 AI 在两周的晚上和周末里做出来。整个 Vue 运行时跑在 Lynx 的后台线程，每个 tick 把 DOM 变更打包成一批送到主线程，让 Vue 应用在 iOS、Android 和 Web 上渲染原生 UI。Vue 上游 949 个测试中，有 852 个通过了这条双线程管线。

commentary.en: When things actually work, you let the demos do the talking.
commentary.zh: 真正做通了，就让 Demo 自己说话。

description.en: I'm the architect of [Lynx](https://lynxjs.org/), the cross-platform UI framework behind TikTok and CapCut, which we [open-sourced](https://github.com/lynx-family/lynx) in March 2025. It lets web skills, React and CSS, drive truly native UI on a dual-threaded runtime, and surfaces moved from web to Lynx often launch two to four times faster.
description.zh: I'm the architect of [Lynx](https://lynxjs.org/), the cross-platform UI framework behind TikTok and CapCut, which we [open-sourced](https://github.com/lynx-family/lynx) in March 2025. It lets web skills, React and CSS, drive truly native UI on a dual-threaded runtime, and surfaces moved from web to Lynx often launch two to four times faster.

commentary.en: Not a better React Native. The bet is that web skills plus a two-thread runtime can unlock native — for more platforms, more products, more people.
commentary.zh: Not a better React Native. The bet is that web skills plus a two-thread runtime can unlock native — for more platforms, more products, more people.

details.en: From the launch post I wrote: "Today, we're excited to introduce Lynx, a family of technologies empowering developers to use their existing web skills to create truly native UIs for both mobile and web from a single codebase. Designed for diverse use cases and rich interactivity, Lynx delivers vibrant and engaging UIs for large-scale apps like TikTok, featuring a speedy, versatile rendering engine, performance-driven dual-threaded UI programming, modern Rust-based tooling, and more!" The family: a dual-threaded runtime on PrimJS, ReactLynx, the Rspack-based Rspeedy toolchain, and Lynx for Web. Apache 2.0.
details.zh: From the launch post I wrote: "Today, we're excited to introduce Lynx, a family of technologies empowering developers to use their existing web skills to create truly native UIs for both mobile and web from a single codebase. The family: a dual-threaded runtime on PrimJS, ReactLynx, the Rspack-based Rspeedy toolchain, and Lynx for Web. Apache 2.0.

description.en: SegmentFault and KAIYUANSHE named me one of 2022's 33 China Open Source Pioneers, for bringing a top open-source team's voice to Chinese developers and carrying React's ideas into China without distortion.
description.zh: 我被 SegmentFault 思否与开源社评为「2022 中国开源先锋 33 人」之一，理由是把顶级开源团队的声音带给国内开发者，无失真地在国内传播 React 的思想。

details.en: The citation: "Xuan Huang, software engineer at Meta on React, an open-source team the internet loves. Why: he brought the voice of a top open-source team to developers in China and helped spread React's ideas here without distortion. Hard-core technically, and good at making deep things simple; the community loves him." Chosen over a month from 72 nominations by SegmentFault, KAIYUANSHE and past pioneers.
details.zh: 「黄玄丨Facebook Meta 签约软件工程师，就职于开源技术网红团队 React。推荐理由：给国内开发者带来了来自顶级开源团队的声音，为在国内无失真地传播 React 相关思想贡献力量。技术硬核而又擅长深入浅出，深受社区小伙伴的喜爱。」评选历时一月有余，共收到 72 份有效报名，由 SegmentFault 思否与开源社的主编团和往届中国开源先锋组成的评审团共同评出。

description.en: At COSCon'22, China's open-source conference, I gave the Chinese community the React team's big picture after React 18: core, web, cross-platform, libraries, frameworks, docs and tools, and how Chinese developers can take part.
description.zh: 在第七届中国开源年会上，以 React 团队一员的视角，给中文社区讲了一遍 React 18 之后的全景：核心、Web、跨平台、库、框架、文档与工具，以及作为中国开发者如何参与。

details.en: From the video's description: "A talk at the 7th China Open Source Conference: from my own understanding, a look back and ahead, from a global perspective, at what has happened and is about to happen across the React ecosystem, covering React core, web, cross-platform, libraries, frameworks, docs and tools, to help you see React's big picture." The submitted outline: 1. Where React stands (React 18). 2. Where React is heading and what it is solving (after React 18). 3. How Chinese developers can take part.
details.zh: 视频简介：「今年年底时在「第七届中国开源年会」上的分享：从我个人的理解，尝试以一种比较「全局性的视角」跟大家一起回顾以及展望一下 React 整个生态这一段时期以来已经发生和将要发生的一些变化，力求涵盖 React 核心、Web、跨平台、库、框架、文档、工具等整个 React 生态的方方面面，希望能对大家理解 React 的整个 big picture 有帮助！」提交的大纲：1. React 现状回顾（React 18 相关）2. React 发展方向和在解决的问题（React 18 之后）3. 作为中国开发者如何参与。

description.en: I talked with Gitee for its cover-story series: from art student at CUC through Alibaba, WePiao, the Ele.me PWA and RIT, to the React Core team, React Forget, and keeping a life outside work.
description.zh: Gitee「封面人物」的一期专访：从广院的艺术生，到阿里、微影、饿了么 PWA 和 RIT，一路聊到 React Core 与 React Forget，以及工作和生活的平衡。

details.en: "React's Xuan Huang: a B-Boy who doesn't get art is no programmer with swag." "A slash youth who knows a little computer science and a little art; now a software engineer at Meta on the open-source React Core Team, and tech lead of the React Forget compiler project."
details.zh: 「React 黄玄：不懂艺术的 B-Boy 不是 Swag 的程序员」。「一个略懂计算机科学与艺术的斜杆不动青年，现 Meta 软件工程师，目前就职于开源技术团队 React Core Team，还是 React Forget 编译器项目 Tech Lead。」

description.en: My React Conf 2021 talk, and React Forget's first public appearance: a demo of an auto-memoizing compiler prototype from React Labs, so you could write React without memo, useMemo and useCallback. Four years later, React Compiler 1.0 [credited it](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/07/react-compiler-1) as the first iteration of the compiler that shipped.
description.zh: My React Conf 2021 talk, and React Forget's first public appearance: a demo of an auto-memoizing compiler prototype from React Labs, so you could write React without memo, useMemo and useCallback. Four years later, React Compiler 1.0 [credited it](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/07/react-compiler-1) as the first iteration of the compiler that shipped.

details.en: From the [conference recap](https://react.dev/blog/2021/12/17/react-conf-2021-recap): "Looking further into the future, Xuan Huang (黄玄) shared an update from our React Labs research into an auto-memoizing compiler. Check out this talk for more information and a demo of the compiler prototype." React Conf 2021 was the first held online, on December 8, 2021, with over 50,000 people registered.
details.zh: From the [conference recap](https://react.dev/blog/2021/12/17/react-conf-2021-recap): "Looking further into the future, Xuan Huang (黄玄) shared an update from our React Labs research into an auto-memoizing compiler. Check out this talk for more information and a demo of the compiler prototype." React Conf 2021 was the first held online, on December 8, 2021, with over 50,000 people registered.

description.en: I worked on [Hermes](https://github.com/facebook/hermes), Meta's JavaScript engine for React Native: language features from Proxy to microtasks, releases 0.6 to 0.9, and Meta's side of bringing it to iOS in React Native 0.64 with Callstack and Microsoft ([we talked about it](https://www.callstack.com/podcasts/react-native-0-64-with-hermes-for-ios-ep-5)). I wrote the roadmap, Toward Hermes being the Default; within a year it was.
description.zh: I worked on [Hermes](https://github.com/facebook/hermes), Meta's JavaScript engine for React Native: language features from Proxy to microtasks, releases 0.6 to 0.9, and Meta's side of bringing it to iOS in React Native 0.64 with Callstack and Microsoft ([we talked about it](https://www.callstack.com/podcasts/react-native-0-64-with-hermes-for-ios-ep-5)). I wrote the roadmap, Toward Hermes being the Default; within a year it was.

details.en: Hermes is an open-source JavaScript engine optimized for running React Native, built around ahead-of-time compilation to compact bytecode. It shipped opt-in on iOS in [React Native 0.64](https://reactnative.dev/blog/2021/03/12/version-0.64) (March 2021) and became the default engine in [React Native 0.70](https://reactnative.dev/blog/2022/09/05/version-070) (September 2022). The roadmap post reported time-to-interactive cut by nearly half, p99.9 GC pauses 34 times shorter with Hades on 64-bit, and a 30% smaller heap.
details.zh: Hermes is an open-source JavaScript engine optimized for running React Native, built around ahead-of-time compilation to compact bytecode. It shipped opt-in on iOS in [React Native 0.64](https://reactnative.dev/blog/2021/03/12/version-0.64) (March 2021) and became the default engine in [React Native 0.70](https://reactnative.dev/blog/2022/09/05/version-070) (September 2022). The roadmap post reported time-to-interactive cut by nearly half, p99.9 GC pauses 34 times shorter with Hades on 64-bit, and a 30% smaller heap.

description.en: I was the founding engineer and tech lead of React Forget on the React Core team: a compiler that memoizes components and hooks for you, so React is fast by default without memo, useMemo and useCallback. I [demoed its first iteration](commit:reactconf-2021-memo) in 2021, and it shipped as [React Compiler 1.0](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/07/react-compiler-1) in 2025.
description.zh: I was the founding engineer and tech lead of React Forget on the React Core team: a compiler that memoizes components and hooks for you, so React is fast by default without memo, useMemo and useCallback. I [demoed its first iteration](commit:reactconf-2021-memo) in 2021, and it shipped as [React Compiler 1.0](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/07/react-compiler-1) in 2025.

commentary.en: The authoring model should stay clean. If memoization is load-bearing, a compiler should do it — so React can be fast by default. We called it Forget; it shipped as React Compiler.
commentary.zh: The authoring model should stay clean. If memoization is load-bearing, a compiler should do it — so React can be fast by default. We called it Forget; it shipped as React Compiler.

details.en: From the React docs: React Compiler "automatically optimizes your React application by handling memoization for you, eliminating the need for manual useMemo, useCallback, and React.memo." From React Labs, June 2022, which I co-authored: "We gave an early preview of React Forget at React Conf 2021. It's a compiler that automatically generates the equivalent of useMemo and useCallback calls to minimize the cost of re-rendering, while retaining React's programming model." From the React Compiler 1.0 post: "In 2021, Xuan Huang demoed the first iteration of a new take on React Compiler."

description.en: My master's capstone at RIT, with [Prof. Matthew Fluet](https://www.cs.rit.edu/~mtf/): the W3C WebAssembly 1.0 spec mechanized in Coq, with an (almost) complete proof that it is sound. Following the standard itself turned up bugs I [fixed upstream](https://github.com/WebAssembly/spec/pull/1093), and the name lives on: Cambridge and Imperial's [WasmCert-Coq](https://github.com/WasmCert/WasmCert-Coq) carries it, with permission.

Following the standard itself turned up bugs I [fixed upstream](https://github.com/WebAssembly/spec/pull/1093), and the name lives on: Cambridge and Imperial's [WasmCert-Coq](https://github.com/WasmCert/WasmCert-Coq) carries it, with permission.

preview.title: A Mechanized Formalization of the WebAssembly Specification in Coq
preview.description: RIT Computer Science · Capstone Report · 2019. A mechanization of the W3C WebAssembly Core Specification 1.0 in Coq, with a machine-checked soundness proof.

commentary.en: 144 pages of W3C spec, about 5,000 lines of Coq. Applying formal verification, we show WebAssembly is safe.
commentary.zh: 144 pages of W3C spec, about 5,000 lines of Coq. Applying formal verification, we show WebAssembly is safe.

details.en: "A Mechanized Formalization of the WebAssembly Specification in Coq", capstone report, RIT Computer Science, Fall 2019. Abstract: "We developed a mechanized formalization of W3C WebAssembly Core Specification 1.0 in the Coq proof assistant, and (almost) completed a mechanized proof that this semantics is sound, implying both its type safety and memory safety. Wasm has been designed and standardized with formal semantics. In contrast to prior work, our mechanized formalization closely follows the standard, exposed issues and provided bug fixes. Our work serves as a foundation for certified software development in the Coq community." Code: [Huxpro/WasmCert](https://github.com/Huxpro/WasmCert). The FM 2021 paper Two Mechanisations of WebAssembly 1.0: "Xuan presents a partial Coq-mechanisation of Wasm in his M.Sc project, independently named WasmCert. We have been given permission to use the WasmCert name."

description.en: A summer 2019 internship at Facebook Reality Labs, on a new programming language and application framework for all-day wearable, low-power devices: part of [XROS](https://www.theverge.com/2022/2/25/22950710/meta-vr-ar-os-team-xros-breakup-hyper-tuned-focus), Meta's own operating system for AR and VR.
description.zh: A summer 2019 internship at Facebook Reality Labs, on a new programming language and application framework for all-day wearable, low-power devices: part of [XROS](https://www.theverge.com/2022/2/25/22950710/meta-vr-ar-os-team-xros-breakup-hyper-tuned-focus), Meta's own operating system for AR and VR.

details.en: How my manager framed it: "As part of Reality Labs Research (formerly Oculus Research), I led a research team building a new programming language and application framework specifically targeting all-day wearable, low power devices." XROS was Meta's effort to build its own OS for its AR and VR devices; The Verge reported in 2022 that the roughly 300-person team had been broken up and embedded into the product lines.

description.en: My first summer at Facebook, in 2018: an internship with the ReasonML team, the OCaml-syntax, type-safe way to write JavaScript, working on Messenger.com, [its biggest production user](https://reasonml.github.io/blog/2017/09/08/messenger-50-reason). Its compiler later became [ReScript](https://rescript-lang.org/).
description.zh: My first summer at Facebook, in 2018: an internship with the ReasonML team, the OCaml-syntax, type-safe way to write JavaScript, working on Messenger.com, [its biggest production user](https://reasonml.github.io/blog/2017/09/08/messenger-50-reason). Its compiler later became [ReScript](https://rescript-lang.org/).

details.en: From its homepage: "Reason lets you write simple, fast and quality type safe code while leveraging both the JavaScript & OCaml ecosystems." Messenger.com was half Reason by 2017, with ten bugs in a year. In 2020 BuckleScript, Reason's JavaScript compiler, took its own syntax and was rebranded ReScript; Reason continues on its own.

description.en: My JSConf China 2017 talk: the Ele.me PWA, distilled into ten steps from "a web app" to "the Web", for upgrading any site into a Progressive Web App. [One attendee](https://new.halfrost.com/jsconf_china_2017_final/) called it one of his two biggest takeaways, alongside Evan You's.
description.zh: JSConf China 2017 上的分享：把饿了么 PWA 的经验，提炼成从「一个 Web App」到「The Web」的十个台阶，教你一步步把任意网站升级成 PWA。

details.en: The ten steps: A Web App, A Standalone Web App, An Installable Web App, An Evergreen Web App, An Offline-1st Web App, A Streaming Web App, A Progressive Web App, A JavaScript Web App, Any Web App/Site, The Web. Talked in Chinese, slides in English. The YouTube recording is gone; the slides still play here, and the conference page survives on the [Wayback Machine](https://web.archive.org/web/20170724044527/http://2017.jsconf.cn/en/).
details.zh: 十个台阶：A Web App、A Standalone Web App、An Installable Web App、An Evergreen Web App、An Offline-1st Web App、A Streaming Web App、A Progressive Web App、A JavaScript Web App、Any Web App/Site、The Web。用中文讲，幻灯片是英文的。YouTube 上的录像已下线；幻灯片仍可在此播放，会议官网留在了 [Wayback Machine](https://web.archive.org/web/20170724044527/http://2017.jsconf.cn/en/) 里。

description.en: I joined Ele.me as a PWA consultant for three months in 2017 to prove that a multi-page Vue app could be a Progressive Web App too. It became the first influential PWA in China: a skeleton painted at 400ms, interactive in about two seconds. I [wrote it up](https://medium.com/elemefe/upgrading-ele-me-to-progressive-web-app-2a446832e509), and drew its architecture for Addy Osmani's Google I/O 2017 talk.
description.zh: 2017 年以 PWA 顾问的身份加入饿了么三个月，想证明一个基于 Vue 的多页应用也能成为 PWA。它成了国内第一个有影响力的 PWA：骨架屏 400ms 首绘，两秒左右可交互。我把它[写成了文章](/writing/upgrading-eleme-to-pwa/zh)，也为 Addy Osmani 在 Google I/O 2017 的演讲画了它的架构图。

details.en: From web.dev: "Ele.me is the biggest food ordering and delivery company in mainland China. It serves 260 million registered users from over 200 cities all around China, and has over 1.3 million restaurant listings. With 99% of its users ordering food on mobile, Ele.me set out to improve its mobile web experience, making it faster and more reliable in flaky connections, all while relying on the core technical model of a multi-page app to accommodate their operational needs." Loading time fell 11.6% across pre-cached pages and 6.35% on average; time-to-consistently-interactive dropped to 4.93 seconds on 3G on first load.

description.en: My bachelor's graduation project: a WYSIWYG presentation tool in the vein of Google Slides, for web slides that are linkable, sharable, cross-platform and need no delivery, betting on the web itself rather than PowerPoint and Keynote. I built my own PWA talks on it, from [QCon 2016](commit:qcon-shanghai-2016) to [JSConf 2017](commit:jsconf-china-2017), and it's still online.
description.zh: 我的本科毕业设计：一个所见即所得的在线演示工具，像 Google Slides，做可链接、可分享、跨平台、无需分发的 Web 幻灯片，押注的是 Web 本身，而不是 PowerPoint 与 Keynote。后来我的 PWA 演讲，从 [QCon 2016](commit:qcon-shanghai-2016) 到 [JSConf 2017](commit:jsconf-china-2017)，都是用它做的。

details.en: Its tagline: "Create truly cross-platform HTML5 presentations, and take what you share to any corner of the world." In my own words at the time: "a online software helping you create, store and share web slides."
details.zh: 「创作真正跨平台的 HTML5 展示文稿，让你的分享到达世界的任何一个角落。」

description.en: At WePiao I was a founding engineer of its movie-ticketing app (then 微票儿, later 娱票儿), and founded and led the company's front-end infrastructure team, which moved the whole company onto React.
description.zh: 在微影时代，我是微票儿（后更名娱票儿）的创始工程师，组建并带领公司的前端基础架构团队，把全公司的技术栈迁到了 React。

details.en: My speaker bio at QCon Shanghai 2016: "former lead of WePiao's front-end infrastructure team". Beijing Weiying (WePiao) was later acquired by Maoyan.
details.zh: QCon 上海 2016 的讲师介绍：「前微票儿·前端基础工程团队负责人」。微影时代后被猫眼收购。

description.en: I joined Alibaba in my sophomore summer on an interaction-design offer, then asked to switch to front-end and stayed a year with the Alitrip team: building offline packages and the hybrid container, [local H5 over virtual domains](/writing/taobao-hybrid-app/zh), and [product notes from the road](/writing/alitrip-strategy/zh).
description.zh: 大二暑假拿着交互设计的 offer 进了阿里，后来私信拔赤转做前端，在航旅前端团队一待就是一年：参与离线包与 Hybrid 容器共建，做[本地 H5 与虚拟域](/writing/taobao-hybrid-app/zh)，也写了些[在路上的产品思考](/writing/alitrip-strategy/zh)。

details.en: "I joined Alibaba as an intern in my sophomore summer on an interaction-designer offer, but found the work too boring, messaged Bachi (a well-known Alibaba front-end engineer) inside the company, switched to front-end, and stayed for my whole junior year." (Gitee cover story, 2022)
details.zh: 「大二暑假还是拿着交互设计师的 offer 进阿里实习的，但是后来觉得工作内容太无聊了，直接在公司内私信了拔赤老师（阿里巴巴知名前端开发工程师）转成了前端，并且一呆就是整个大三。」（Gitee 封面人物，2022）

description.en: The Jekyll theme and blog a generation of Chinese front-end engineers forked: [7.6k stars and 6.5k forks](https://github.com/Huxpro/huxpro.github.io), the most-starred Jekyll theme by a Chinese author on GitHub, with plenty of forks of forks. Later it became a PWA, too.
description.zh: 被一代中国前端工程师 fork 过的 Jekyll 主题与个人博客：[7.6k 星、6.5k fork](https://github.com/Huxpro/huxpro.github.io)，是 GitHub 上星标最多的中国作者 Jekyll 主题，还有不少「fork 的 fork」。后来它也成了一个 PWA。

commentary.en: 要做一个有 swag 的程序员. The theme was the first thing a lot of people knew me for — before compilers, before Lynx.
commentary.zh: 要做一个有 swag 的程序员。在编译器、在 Lynx 之前，很多人是先从这套主题认识我的。

details.en: "The original Jekyll blog and theme, preserved at huxpro.github.io. For Hux's current website, visit hux.pro." PWA and Service Worker support since V1.7.
details.zh: "The original Jekyll blog and theme, preserved at huxpro.github.io. For Hux's current website, visit hux.pro." V1.7 起支持 PWA / Service Worker。

description.en: An internal talk at WePiao that escaped the building: JavaScript modules told in seven days, from design patterns through script loaders, CommonJS, AMD/CMD and Browserify/Webpack to ES6 modules. Shared on Weibo, it was reposted by about 200 people including Evan You and read 100,000 times; [its repo](https://github.com/Huxpro/js-module-7day) still has over 600 stars.
description.zh: 在微票儿的一次内部分享，用七天讲完 JavaScript 模块化：从设计模式、script loader、CommonJS、AMD/CMD、Browserify/Webpack 一路到 ES6 Module。发到微博后被尤雨溪等近 200 人转发、阅读 10 万，[仓库](https://github.com/Huxpro/js-module-7day)至今 600 多星。

details.en: Day 1, Module? (it starts with design patterns). Day 2, Script Loader (encapsulation isn't enough, we need loading). Day 3, Module Loader (the industrial revolution of modular architecture). Day 4, CommonJS (conquering the world starts outside the browser). Day 5, AMD/CMD (modules for the browser). Day 6, Browserify/Webpack (the way things are going: drop the wrapper!). Day 7, ES6 Module (the last battle). [Write-up, in Chinese](https://huxpro.github.io/2015/07/09/js-module-7day/).
details.zh: 第一日 上古时期 Module?（从设计模式说起）；第二日 石器时代 Script Loader（只有封装性可不够，我们还需要加载）；第三日 蒸汽朋克 Module Loader（模块化架构的工业革命）；第四日 号角吹响 CommonJS（征服世界的第一步是跳出浏览器）；第五日 双塔奇兵 AMD/CMD（浏览器环境模块化方案）；第六日 精灵宝钻 Browserify/Webpack（大势所趋，去掉这层包裹！）；第七日 王者归来 ES6 Module（最后的战役）。[文字版](https://huxpro.github.io/2015/07/09/js-module-7day/)。

title.zh: 都 2015 年了，CSS 怎么还是这么糟糕

description.en: A tour from OOCSS, SMACSS and BEM to CSS in JS and CSS Modules, ending with my own proposal, [POCss](https://huxpro.github.io/2015/12/28/css-sucks-2015/): scope styles to components, and let pages override them where it makes sense.
description.zh: 从 OOCSS、SMACSS、BEM 讲到 CSS in JS 与 CSS Modules，最后给出我自己的方案 [POCss](https://huxpro.github.io/2015/12/28/css-sucks-2015/)：组件样式要隔离，页面可以合理覆盖。

details.en: "POCss: Page Override Components CSS. 1. Scoping Components: CSS Blocks should only be used inside a component of the same name. 2. Components can be Overrode by Pages." "It's technology-agnostic… Solving problems, and easy… Leverage the power of cascading properly… Scoping components but allow reasonable overriding… It's pragmatic, flexible and hitting the sweet spot."

title.en: Progressive Web App, in my points of view

description.en: At GDG Beijing's Google I/O Redux, fresh from attending I/O 2016, I walked through installability, the app shell, offline, service workers and re-engagement, and was honest about the downsides. A field note from the year before Ele.me's PWA.
description.zh: GDG 北京的 Google I/O Redux 上，刚从 I/O 2016 回来，讲 PWA 的可安装、App Shell、离线、Service Worker 与再参与，也老实讲了它的短板。是饿了么 PWA 之前一年的田野笔记。

title.en: Progressive Web App, Make Web Great Again
title.zh: Progressive Web App, 复兴序章

description.en: At QCon Shanghai 2016, in a front-end track that also had Evan You on Vue 2.0, I introduced Progressive Web Apps to Chinese developers: the web's counterattack on native.
description.zh: QCon 上海 2016 前端技术实践专场（同场还有尤雨溪的 Vue 2.0），我把 PWA 介绍给国内开发者：来自 Web 阵营、对 Native 的一次反击。

details.en: Official title, "Progressive Web App: the counterattack begins". The abstract: "The war between native and web has not let up since the day the web was born, and in the mobile era it has only grown fiercer, fought over a few square inches. Some stand firmly with native; others keep the open web as their faith. As convergence became the mainstream, hybrid, dynamic and web-paradigm cross-platform solutions flourished, and the Google Chrome team, together with Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, Opera and other browser vendors, gave the web's answer: Progressive Web Apps, sounding the counterattack against native… This talk covers everything you need to know about PWA :)"
details.zh: 官方题目「Progressive Web App：反击序章」。摘要：「关于 Native 与 Web 的纷争，从 Web 诞生之日起到现在就从未消停过。眼看这场战火在移动时代的方寸之间愈演愈烈，有的人坚定地站在了 Native 阵营，有的人则选择 Open Web 作为自己的信仰。近年来，随着融合与相互借鉴的声音成为主流，Hybrid、动态化与基于 Web 开发范式的跨平台解决方案百花齐放，而 Google Chrome 团队，也联合 Microsoft Edge、Mozilla Firefox、Opera 等一众浏览器厂商，给出了来自 Web 阵营的回应——Progressive Web App，向 Native 阵营吹响了反击的号角……本次分享将涵盖：关于 PWA 你需要知道的一切 ：）」

title.en: Going home? Switching jobs? Taking time off? — Late-night reflections from a ten-year coder
